correctness.rationale: For the edge-as-object/vertex-as-attribute formal context of any finite simple undirected graph n≥3, minimum degree at least 2, two distinct edges share at most one endpoint. Hence closed extents are exactly bottom ∅, m singleton edges, n distinct incident-edge stars S_v, and E, for m+n+2 concepts. Stability of a star is (2^{d(v)}−1−d(v))/2^{d(v)}, because at least two selected incident edges are necessary and sufficient to derive singleton v; top bad subsets are empty, m singletons and disjoint families of star subsets of cardinality≥2. Thus top stability 1−(Σ_v 2^{d(v)}−n−m+1)/2^m. Coatoms are vertex stars, and their meet is the atom {uv} iff uv is an edge; unlabelled lattice alone reconstructs G. K_{3,3} and triangular prism each have six vertices, nine edges, degree3; for t copies all mixtures are nonisomorphic (triangle count distinguishes) while identical degree multisets give identical spectra. Independently rebuilt both six-vertex incidence contexts and confirmed exact 17-value multiset 1, fifteen 1/2, 239/256.

value.rationale: The concept lattice retains an incidence graph completely through its order, while the entire distribution of the widely used concept-stability statistic provably forgets adjacency and suffers arbitrarily large nonisomorphic collisions. This mathematically motivated information-loss statement is stronger than computing a stability formula for one graph and useful for evaluating stability as a representation or selection invariant.
